reason: The checker question is 'what TypeKind set (any / number / enum / string / boolean / null / undefined / object) does each operand's type resolve to, including aliases, generics, enums and unions?'. With the options as overrides, the port is exact whenever both operands are literals (76/90, 0 FP). Every miss has an identifier or enum-member operand whose kind comes from a declaration, and the same syntax with another declared type is valid. Checker APIs: getTypeAtLocation of both operands and their flag sets (:131-132). Line 52 needs an unconstrained generic, line 112 a string enum.

evidence.why: `return a === b;` with `a: T` (unconstrained generic -> object) is flagged; line 56 has the identical `return a === b;` with `a: any` and is valid
`c1 === c2` is flagged because c1/c2 are declared `myObject` (alias of Object); `b1 === b2` (line 70, alias of string) is the same syntax and valid

`h1 > h2` with `string | number` declarations resolves to string ordering
